ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the diagonals AC and BD of the square ABCD intersect at point O, and OA = 3. What is the area of this square?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the square ABCD, with OA=3,\\
it follows that AC=BD=6, and AO$\perp$BO,\\
hence the area of the square is: $\frac{1}{2}$AC$\times$BD=$\boxed{18}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a square ABCD with both diagonals AC and BD drawn crossing at O. From the text, use OA = 3. Since O is the intersection point of the diagonals of a square, it is the midpoint of diagonal AC, so AC = 2·OA = 6. In a square the diagonals are equal and perpendicular, so BD = AC = 6 and AC ⟂ BD. Compute the square's area using the rhombus/square diagonal-area formula: area = (1/2)·AC·BD = (1/2)·6·6 = 18.
